decisions.reason: As a close-to-core delivery offer in a growing market, it is easy for management to justify keeping it while attributing any early frictions to ramp-up and capacity tuning rather than to a flawed concept.

The seventy-two-hour promise is more operationally demanding and therefore somewhat more droppable than other launches, but escalation of commitment and its fit with the firm's service-oriented positioning still favor continuation.
This door is highly visible, technically certified, and tightly aligned with the firm's safety-focused core business, so prior development effort and public commitment make withdrawal unlikely.
A dedicated express product line with several models signals meaningful resource commitment and public positioning, which under an escalation logic strongly supports keeping it on the market.

The digital ordering and service platform fits the firm's stated move toward deeper advisory and service support, and the sunk investment plus strategic centrality make management very likely to persist.

Because it extends the established fire-protection offering and supports the firm's compliance-and-safety value proposition, management would be inclined to continue it unless results were clearly poor.
